items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I heard Nat King Cole one day something struck me... That’s the music I like.

ctx.x: Right. So musicians talk about, especially in the older vernacular about paying dues. And it’s clear to me you’ve paid some dues simply to get here in the States, but before that I’m wondering was there any question about what your livelihood was going to be even before you came to the United States? At what point did you decide I’m going to be a musician?

That was early. That was early, during my childhood. I decided that I wanted to be a musician when I was eleven years old. When I was eleven years old my father came to our apartment with two albums, one by the Nat King Cole Trio and the second one was the Glenn Miller Orchestra with Gene Krupa on drums. By that time I was studying the violin, because my father used to play the violin and my mother wanted me to be like my dad. So I started fooling around with the violin and went to the National School of the Arts…
Did you study Mozart and the European composers on the violin?
